description:
PROBLEM TYPE: LP

PROBLEM INFO: 
- Consider a set \var{P} described by linear inequality constraints, that is:
 \var{P} = {\var{x} \in R^\var{N} | \var{a_i}^T x <= \var{b_i} , i = 1, ..., m}.

where \var{a_i} \in R^\var{N} and \var{b_i} \in R

- A ball with center \var{y} in R^\var{N} and radius \var{r} is defined as the set of all points within (Euclidean) distance \var{r} from \var{y}.


INPUT FORMAT: 

{
    "A": [[a_i_j for j in 1, ..., n] for i in 1, ..., m],
    "b": [b_i for i in 1, ..., m]
}

OBJECTIVE: We are interested in finding a ball with the largest possible radius, which is entirely contained within the set \var{P} (The center of such a ball is called the Chebychev center of \var{P}.

OUTPUT INFO:

- center (list): The center of the ball as a list of floats of length \var{N}
- radius (float): The radius of the ball as a float

OUTPUT FORMAT:

{
    "center": [y_j for j in 1, ..., n],
    "radius": r
}

M.definition: The number of inequalities defining the set P

N.definition: The ambient space dimension of the set P

A.definition: The coefficients of the linear inequalities defining the set P

B.definition: The right-hand side of the inequalities defining the set P

objective.description: "Maximize the radius of a ball that is entirely contained within the polyhedral set P (i.e., find the Chebyshev center by maximizing the inscribed ball radius)"

constraints.description: For each i = 1, ..., M: a_i^T y + r * ||a_i||_2 <= b_i
constraints.formulation: $\\forall i = 1, \\dots, M:\\; \\sum_{j=1}^{N} A[i,j] \\, y[j] + r \\sqrt{\\sum_{j=1}^{N} A[i,j]^2} \\leq B[i]$

r.definition: The radius of the ball contained in the set P
